outcomes: A user or agent serves a workload together with the workloads it runs with in one command, and every one of them is reachable at a URL that stays the same across restarts
A workload that declares a database gets its own, migrated by the workload at boot, without anyone starting a server or copying a connection string
A composition that died without tearing itself down leaves nothing behind once the next one starts
A change's execution proof is one command whose smoke is derived from the workload's own route inventory, never improvised
A deployed environment is qualified only when it reports the build the caller expects
Anything short of a proven pass reads as a failure to every caller, human or automated
nonGoals: Inferring what a workload runs with from its dependency graph
Deploying, scaling or supervising workloads beyond one developer machine
Running migrations on behalf of a workload
Printing or recording the injected configuration

requirements.text: compose serves the transitive runsWith closure of one project in topological order, reading each runsWith list from the workspace membership of its job context: the list putnami.json authors, else the one the provider reported, such as a TypeScript package.json's putnami.runsWith. A library, image, unknown or cyclic member, or one whose configuration disables serve, is refused before anything starts.

Each member of a composition runs behind a 127.0.0.1 proxy whose URL is known before any process starts and answers 503 until the member announces a port. A dependant receives each provider's proxy URL under its client-contract service id and its project name.

Each datasource a member declares in infra/requirements.json is bound through the database config section. On a provider that isolates, it gets a database named compose_<id>_<slug>_<datasource>, recorded in the lease before it is created and dropped when the composition stops; on a provided server members share its database and the composition reports isolation none.

A member is ready when its serve step emits a typed v2 ready event; the proxy forwards to the first http or https endpoint port, else the first endpoint port, of the latest claim that carries one, and a claim without an endpoint leaves it where it was. A member starts only once the one before it is ready. A member that exits first, or stays silent past --ready-timeout, fails the composition with a code naming the member and the phase, and everything already started is torn down.

A composition keeps a lease under .putnami/compose/<id> with its pid, member process groups, database names, provisioner digest and proxy ports. The next composition reaps every lease whose lock is free and whose pid is dead: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after two seconds, drops the databases, removes the lease, and reports each reap.

Service URLs and database bindings reach a member only through CONFIG_DATA on its serve step, never through a file in the project tree or a cache key. Output, errors and the lease carry section and datasource names, never the document, a connection string or a password. A member whose environment already carries CONFIG_DATA is refused.

The contract is read from schema/http-routes.json, then .gen/schema/http-routes.json, with the strict inventory parser. Without --platform-prefix, the prefix is where the inventory declares GET readyz and version.

A workload with no route inventory, or with no request safe to derive, yields a verdict of unsupported that opens no target, never passed. A missing inventory names `putnami build --projects <id>` as the remedy. --print-contract still prints the empty contract and exits 0.
A URL target requires --expect-sha, a lowercase hexadecimal sha of at least 7 characters; without it the command exits 2. A target with credentials, a query or a fragment is refused.

--target local composes the workload with the workloads it runs with, production-mode without watch, and reads the worktree fingerprint before anything is prepared. --expect-sha with local exits 2. A composition failure is composition_failed naming the member and phase; teardown always runs and cleanup.state is recorded.

A production compose member, which is every member under --target local, runs the production build with the local config: it receives APP_ENV=local unless the caller exported APP_ENV, so it reads conf/.env.local.yaml and conf/.secrets.local.yaml as under serve, and a workload that needs a local secret to start qualifies.

Go and TypeScript applications report completed startup, once every plugin starter and module start hook returned, two ways: a typed v2 ready event with target workload, which compose records per member, and a platform /readyz that answers 200 only from then on. --target local polls GET <prefix>/readyz when the inventory declares it or --platform-prefix is set, else waits for the claim; a server claim never counts. No claim in time is timed_out with no request sent; an early exit is composition_failed.

Exit 0 follows passed alone. Every other verdict state exits 1 and still delivers the verdict: human output prints it, and --output=json carries it as the failure envelope's data. A request answering 500 or above fails the smoke without stopping the other requests.

compose runs each member as `putnami serve --projects <member> --port 0 --serve-env - --output=jsonl` of the putnami that launched it, without PUTNAMI_INTERACTIVE, with --no-watch unless it is the watched target, and with the invocation's --verbose, --quiet and --no-color; a structured run always adds --no-color. Its environment document arrives on stdin and reaches only its serve step, never a session file. The start, exit, failure and verdict documents keep their bytes.

compose reads each serve run's session stream for the serve step's process group, its readiness claims and its end. A run that fails before its serve step starts is compose.prepare_failed, and --ready-timeout and readyMs count from the serve step's start, so the run's finite steps never count against them. A member reports how its serve last ended: the serve step's own end, else the run's exit, never a step the run canceled to replace it.

compose passes each serve run's stderr through and keeps its last lines for a failure. qualify passes it through only in a verbose human run; otherwise it writes on stderr only the output of the step that failed a run before its serve step, from the session stream: that step's log events, diagnostics and error, or the run's last lines when no step failed.

The lease records each serve run's process group and each serve step's, with their leaders' start times, so the next invocation reaps both. Teardown stops the members' runs in reverse start order, then the proxies, the databases and the lease, within 75s, so it ends before putnami kills the command 90s after a signal; it waits for a killed run no longer than that.

On Unix, compose and qualify watch the putnami process that launched them. Once it is gone, even killed outright, they notice within a second and tear down as on a terminal signal, and a write to a stdout or stderr without a reader never ends them. On Windows, putnami's Job Object ends them and every serve run they started with putnami, without a teardown, and the next composition reaps the lease.

The @putnami/dev manifest declares the compose and qualify command groups at CLI contract 15. Each defaults to its only subcommand, up and run, which is interactive and takes the project as a required positional, so putnami compose <project> and putnami qualify <project> run it. compose-up declares the serve workload and qualify-run the once workload, so no portable or commit-addressed run carries either. Their tasks run the dev executable in the workspace root, uncached and without a deadline.

The dev executable reads the workspace membership and the output flags --verbose, --quiet and --no-color from the job context putnami appends, and starts each serve run with the absolute putnami executable PUTNAMI_CLI_EXECUTABLE names. A launch without either fails with exit status 1 before anything starts, and a usage error exits 2. A hosted run refuses both groups.

putnami writes each warning of the workspace load that launches compose or qualify once on stderr, unless --quiet, and hands the warnings to the dev executable in the job context's workspaceWarnings. Every result envelope compose and qualify write, a usage error's and a failure's included, carries them in workspaceWarnings, and neither command writes them on stderr again. A load that warned of nothing hands no member, and no envelope carries one.
